## Discovery & Translational Science

**Elevenostat demonstrated to be off-target for HDAC11** [Science.org](https://www.science.org/content/blog-post/elevenostat-don-t-believe-label)
* Re-evaluation of elevenostat, long utilized as an HDAC11-selective probe, demonstrates only weak binding to HDAC11 (~10 μM).
* The molecule exhibits single-digit nanomolar affinity for HDAC6 and HDAC10, indicating its cellular activity is mediated primarily through these off-target deacetylases.

**Dual GIP/GLP-2 agonist GL-0001 reduces bone fragility in osteogenesis imperfecta model** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.16.759580)
* GL-0001, a first-in-class dual GIP and GLP-2 receptor agonist, was evaluated over 9 weeks in the *oim/oim* mouse model of severe osteogenesis imperfecta.
* Treatment enhanced bone material properties and reduced bone fragility compared to saline and zoledronic acid.

**Pre-infusion T-cell phenotypes predict response duration to anti-CD19 CAR-T therapy** [Nature Medicine](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04707-w)
* A multi-trial cohort analysis of non-Hodgkin lymphoma patients treated with anti-CD19 CAR-T cell therapies identified pre-infusion product composition as a key biomarker of outcome.
* High proportions of naive-like and stem cell memory-like CCR7⁺CD45RA⁺ T cells in the autologous product correlated significantly with prolonged clinical response.

**IBDex frozen transcriptomic atlas created for mucosal bulk RNA-seq in IBD** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.20.26365993)
* IBDex was constructed from 3,168 intestinal biopsies across 1,680 patients using a tissue-aware conditional variational autoencoder trained on a 3,000-gene interface.
* Without parameter updates, the frozen atlas successfully executed anatomy-conditioned gene-response mapping across unseen IBD cohorts and trial data for olamkicept.

**Multi-omic profiling links plasma AD biomarkers to disease progression modules** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.14.26360394)
* A study in 484 adults mapped clinical blood biomarkers (Aβ42/40, p-tau181, p-tau217, GFAP, NfL) across >6,000 plasma proteins.
* Linear modeling defined specific, overlapping proteomic signatures and cellular pathways tracking systemic pathology across cognitive stages.

**Renal GDF15 acts as a required regulator against hypokalemia in primary aldosteronism** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.18.759915)
* Patients with primary aldosteronism displayed a 3-fold elevation in urinary GDF15 and a 1.6-fold increase in plasma GDF15, which normalized post-treatment.
* Murine mineralocorticoid excess models confirmed that GDF15 drives type A intercalated cell proliferation and collecting duct K⁺ reabsorption to prevent severe hypokalemia.

## Early Trials — Phase I–II

**[Biotech]** **Tango Therapeutics reports 82% ORR for vopimetostat combination in advanced pancreatic cancer** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/23/esmo-2026-trial-results-tango-therapeutics-vopimetostat-revolution-medicines-rasonque/) | [X / @BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2113580062339404119)
* Tango Therapeutics presented Phase 1/2 clinical data at ESMO 2026 evaluating vopimetostat in combination with Revolution Medicines' daraxonrasib (rasonque) in second- and third-line pancreatic cancer.
* The targeted combination achieved an 82% overall response rate (ORR) and an 88% 9-month progression-free survival (PFS) rate in a biomarker-defined subset of patients with advanced pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, with median PFS not yet reached.

**[Biotech]** **Alnylam presents early clinical data for Huntington's disease siRNA brezosiran** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/23/huntingtons-alnylam-gene-silencing-brezosiran/)
* Early-stage trial results for brezosiran, an investigational RNAi therapeutic targeting the huntingtin gene, demonstrated target knockdown in patients with Huntington's disease.
* Further study is required to establish whether target reduction translates to slowed clinical disease progression.

**[Biotech]** **Invikafusp alfa demonstrates preliminary activity across solid tumors in START-001 trial** [Nature Medicine](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04711-0)
* Invikafusp alfa, a first-in-class bispecific agonistic antibody selectively targeting Vβ6/Vβ10 T cell subsets, met safety endpoints in the Phase 1/2 START-001 trial.
* The agent established a recommended Phase 2 dose and generated early efficacy signals in both immunologically hot and cold solid tumors.

**[Biotech]** **AMPLIFY-7P trial of mKRAS amphiphile vaccine misses primary DFS endpoint** [Nature Medicine](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04734-7)
* The randomized Phase 2 AMPLIFY-7P trial evaluated an off-the-shelf lymph node-targeting mKRAS peptide vaccine (ELI-002) post-curative intent therapy in mKRAS pancreatic cancer.
* While the study did not meet its primary endpoint of disease-free survival (DFS) in the overall population, prespecified subgroup analyses showed significant DFS improvement in ctDNA-negative patients and those without prior radiotherapy.

**24-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine evaluated in Phase 1 and 2 trials** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42908339/)
* Two randomized, double-blind Phase 1 and Phase 2 trials evaluated the safety and immunogenicity of a novel 24-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV24) in healthy Chinese adults.
* Results demonstrated a favorable safety profile and robust serotype-specific immune responses across evaluated dose cohorts.

**[Biotech]** **Zai Lab reports ES-SCLC data for zocilurtatug pelitecan** [X / @BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2113580543509959063)
* Zai Lab presented clinical results for zocilurtatug pelitecan in first-line extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC).
* The asset demonstrated high overall response rates, durable efficacy, and a well-tolerated safety profile.

## Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

**[Big Pharma]** **Moderna and Merck release Phase 3 intismeran autogene data amid ESMO embargo breach** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/moderna-merck-esmo-intismeran-melanoma-vaccine-results/833765/) | [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/22/esmo-moderna-merck-cancer-vaccine-intismeran-data-released/) | [X / @JacobPlieth](https://x.com/JacobPlieth/status/2113374550310240432)
* Detailed Phase 3 trial data presented at ESMO 2026 showed that intismeran autogene combined with Keytruda reduced the risk of recurrence or death by 42% compared to Keytruda monotherapy in resected high-risk melanoma.
* An early embargo breach prompted ESMO organizers to pull distributed materials and halt further embargoed content distribution.
* Shares of both companies fell (including ~17% for Moderna) following the presentation as investors weighed commercial expectations and potential efficacy waning relative to Phase 2 data.

**[Big Pharma]** **AbbVie's lutikizumab meets Phase 3 primary endpoint in hidradenitis suppurativa but misses market targets** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/22/abbvie-lutikizumab-hidradenitis-suppurativa-drug-phase-3-results/)
* AbbVie announced top-line Phase 3 results for lutikizumab, a dual IL-1α/β neutralising antibody, in patients with moderate-to-severe hidradenitis suppurativa.
* The trial achieved statistical significance on its primary efficacy endpoint versus placebo, though the overall magnitude of clinical response fell below financial analyst expectations.

**[Biotech]** **Final Phase 3 analysis confirms efficacy of atacicept in IgA nephropathy** [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2610103)
* Final efficacy results from the Phase 3 trial of atacicept, a dual BAFF/APRIL inhibitor, in patients with IgA nephropathy were published in the New England Journal of Medicine.
* The study confirmed sustained reductions in proteinuria and preservation of eGFR compared to placebo over the complete study follow-up period.

**[Biotech]** **Phase 3 results published for sibeprenlimab in IgA nephropathy** [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2609127)
* Final Phase 3 trial results for sibeprenlimab, a humanized monoclonal antibody targeting APRIL, demonstrated significant reductions in proteinuria relative to placebo in patients with IgA nephropathy.

**[Biotech]** **Agios reports Phase 3 RISE UP trial results for mitapivat in sickle cell disease** [The Lancet](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)01480-7/fulltext)
* The Phase 3, randomized, double-blind RISE UP trial evaluated oral pyruvate kinase activator mitapivat in patients with sickle cell disease.
* Mitapivat achieved statistically significant improvements in hemoglobin concentration and secondary markers of hemolysis compared to placebo.

## Regulatory & Approvals

**FDA launches Neuroscience Advancement and Innovation Nexus (NAIN) to speed neuro-product development** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-launches-new-program-advance-neuroscience-medical-product-development) | [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/industry/neuroscience-advancement-and-innovation-nexus-nain)
* The FDA introduced NAIN, an agency-wide platform uniting CBER, CDER, and CDRH to standardize regulatory scientific tools and trial design frameworks for central nervous system disorders.
* NAIN's inaugural project, the Alzheimer's Prevention Accelerator, will focus specifically on regulatory science and endpoint validation for interventions targeted at preclinical or early-stage cognitive decline.

**[Big Pharma]** **FDA grants traditional approval to Merck's pembrolizumab for TMB-H solid tumors** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/resources-information-approved-drugs/fda-grants-traditional-approval-pembrolizumab-or-pembrolizumab-and-berahyaluronidase-alfa-pmph)
* The FDA converted the accelerated approval of pembrolizumab (Keytruda) and pembrolizumab/berahyaluronidase alfa-pmph (Keytruda Qlex) to traditional approval for unresectable or metastatic tumor mutational burden-high (TMB-H) solid tumors.
* The decision updates the approved indication threshold from ≥10 mutations/megabase to ≥13 mutations/megabase as determined by an FDA-authorized diagnostic test.

**[Biotech]** **FDA accepts Biohaven's resubmitted NDA for troriluzole in spinocerebellar ataxia** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/biohaven-troriluzole-vyglxia-sca-fda-accept-application/833703/)
* The FDA accepted Biohaven's resubmitted New Drug Application for troriluzole (Vyglxia) for the treatment of spinocerebellar ataxia (SCA).
* The agency plans to convene an Advisory Committee meeting to review the resubmission, with a target PDUFA action expected in Q1 2027.

**FDA finalizes guidance on Prescription Drug Use-Related Software (PDURs)** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/22/fda-pdurs-guidance-dtx-telehealth-glp1-addiction-health-tech/)
* The FDA released final guidance detailing regulatory policies for software applications distributed by or on behalf of drug sponsors for use alongside prescription drugs.
* The framework establishes clear boundaries for digital therapeutics, adherence software, and telehealth software accompanying drug treatments.

**Compounding pharmacy issues voluntary Class II recall for copycat tirzepatide** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/glp1-obesity-drug-recall-apothecary-tirzepatide-zepbound/833712/)
* Apothecary Pharma initiated a voluntary Class II recall covering 22 lots of compounded tirzepatide due to an inability to guarantee sterility and safety specifications.
* The recall affects compounding lots with beyond-use dates through late November 2026 amid ongoing legal enforcement by original manufacturers.

**FDA announces public meeting on Rare Disease Framework Initiative** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/news-events/fda-meetings-conferences-and-workshops/fda-rare-disease-framework-initiative-public-meeting-10282026)
* The FDA, in partnership with the Reagan-Udall Foundation, will host a hybrid public meeting on October 28, 2026, to collect input on its Rare Disease Framework Initiative.
* The program aims to modernize rare disease drug development by tailoring regulatory evaluation to disease nuances, patient needs, product modalities, and achievable trial evidence in small populations.

## Business & Strategy

**[Biotech]** **Lycia Therapeutics prices $318 million initial public offering** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/lycia-therapeutics-targeted-protein-degraders-ipo-pricing/833624/)
* Targeted protein degradation company Lycia Therapeutics raised $318 million in an upsized IPO, selling approximately 3 million more shares than projected.
* The company's LYTAC platform targets extracellular and membrane-bound proteins for lysosomal degradation; trading begins on Nasdaq under the ticker "LYCA."

**[Big Pharma]** **Gilead Sciences settles Texas Medicaid kickback litigation for $45 million** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/pharmalot/2026/10/22/gilead-settles-kickback-lawsuit-texas-attorney-general/)
* Gilead agreed to pay $45 million to resolve claims brought by the Texas Attorney General alleging the company paid improper remunerations to influence clinician prescribing habits under Texas Medicaid.

**[Big Pharma]** **Roche maintains 2026 financial outlook despite revenue distortions** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/roche-3q-2026-earnings-sales-outlook/833864/)
* Roche reported a 7% increase in Q3 group sales to 16.1 billion Swiss francs (~$19.6 billion), slightly ahead of consensus.
* Analysts noted the top-line beat was aided by the operational rollout of an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system; Roche maintained its full-year mid-single-digit sales growth target.

**US Treasury considers outbound investment restrictions on Chinese biotech sector** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/22/biotech-news-treasury-restrictions-for-us-investment-in-chinese-biotech/)
* The US Department of the Treasury is preparing proposed rulemaking that would impose additional oversight and potential restrictions on US capital investments and outbound cross-border licensing deals involving Chinese biotechs.

**[Big Pharma]** **Roche licenses preclinical trispecific T-cell engager ZW209 from Zymeworks** [X / @JacobPlieth](https://x.com/JacobPlieth/status/2113577091539288253)
* Roche entered into a global licensing and collaboration agreement for Zymeworks' ZW209, a preclinical trispecific T-cell engager targeting DLL3 × CD28 × CD3.
* Zymeworks will receive $55M upfront and a $40M payment upon initiation of a Phase 1b trial, marking Roche's third clinical or preclinical commitment targeting DLL3.

**[Biotech]** **Zai Lab secures $250M PIPE financing** [X / @BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2113438865188954531)
* Zai Lab completed a $250M private investment in public equity (PIPE) financing at $22.04 per American Depositary Share (ADS).
* The transaction was led by TCGX, with participation from ADAR1 Capital, Balyasny Asset Management, Cormorant, Frazier Life Sciences, RA Capital, RTW Investments, Sirenia Capital, Wellington Management, and Woodline Partners.

## Public Health & Policy

**HHS expert panel outlines ten strategic priorities for human microbiome research** [Nature Medicine](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04730-x)
* An international panel convened by the US Department of Health and Human Services published a consensus policy framework setting ten strategic priorities for integrating microbiome science into chronic disease management and public health.

**White House MAHA adviser resigns ahead of midterm elections** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/22/calley-means-resigns-white-house-adviser-maha-movement/) | [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/22/ultra-processed-food-definition-maha-white-house/)
* Calley Means resigned as top adviser to the White House Make America Healthy Again (MAHA) initiative.
* The departure coincides with public health pressure on the administration to establish a formal federal definition for ultra-processed foods.

**Worth watching:** The market reaction and upcoming regulatory discussions around Phase 3 cancer vaccine long-term durability following the ESMO data disclosures for Moderna and Merck's intismeran autogene.
